paper_metadata.title: Effects of Carbon, Nickel, and Molybdenum on the High Temperature Strength of Fe-Cr-Ni Alloys

evidence.quote: In order to design a new kind of high-temperature Fe-Cr-Ni alloy with good weldability which could be used as structural material of Iron-ore sintering furnaces and Magnesium-smelting tanks, effects of additions of carbon, nickel, and molybdenum to Fe-Cr-Ni alloy on strength at 12500C have been studied.

attributes.morphology: fine and obtuse, precipitated on grain boundaries

evidence.quote: M23C6 carbide is the main type of carbides in the tested Fe-Cr-Ni alloys in which the minimum Cr/C ratio is greater that 40.0
in the high carbon content alloy (0.64%), however, carbides, especially those along GBs, are coarse, and GBs are not so zig-zag as that of medium carbon content alloy.
Austenite has also a f.c.c structure. Otherwise, ferrite has a b.c.c structure
Otherwise, ferrite has a b.c.c structure, and there is no special crystal orientation between ferrite and M23C6 carbides.
too much molybdenum added to the alloy hinders the austenite formation and stability, and promotes the trasformation of M23C6 carbides to M6C one
carbides in the alloy containing medium carbon content (0.36%) are fine, and their distribution results in apparent zigzag of GBs
The rupture strength at high-temperature of the alloy is mainly determined by grain-boundaries.
All tested specimens show the brittle fracture
a great amount of carbides with bad morphology precipitates along GBs (see Figs. 2 and 7) which can cause a large stress concentration, and results in the formation of micro-crevices
If grain-boundaries of the alloy are weaker than grain matrix, when the alloy sample is exerted on a tensile stress, the initial micro-crevices will expand along grain-boundaries
Carbon can increase the high-temperature strength of Fe–Cr–Ni through the combined effects of precipitation strengthening by fine intragranular and intergranular carbides
The zigzag of GBs increases the resistance to the slip of dislocations(7). So the strength of GBs gets improved.
When too much carbon was added in to the alloy, carbides begins coarsening, and a great amount of carbides with bad morphology precipitates along GBs
A certain amount of nickel soluting in the alloy promotes austenite's formation and stabilization, as well as carbon's precipitation, so both the alloy matrix and GBs get strengthened.
Molybdenum can also solute in to carbides, inhibit their solution at high temperature, increases the alloy recrystallization temperature.
